title: minimum-viable-dedicated-plan-and-sensitivity-worksheet
content:
POC: Minimum Viable Dedicated Plan + Sensitivity Worksheet
Customer: Meridian Health (hipothetical POC)
Owner: Daniel Lee (solutions-eng)
Contributors: Priya K., Evan B., Lina G.
Status: draft - working session notes and quick sims

Purpose
- Produce a compact, conservative Dedicated capacity proposal that meets the customer's p95 latency and throughput targets for a Phase 1 POC while minimizing up-front reserved commit.
- Provide an explicit autoscale+fallback policy and a sensitivity table showing monthly GPU spend across realistic demand curves.

POC Goals / Success Criteria\- p95 generation latency <= 450ms for 2k token prompts (model/runner baseline: quantized Llama-3-ish 70B variant)\- Sustained throughput: 180 QPS at 50 tokens per request (burst to 400 QPS for <= 30s)\- Error rate < 0.5% (time-outs/retries) during normal ops\- Monthly committed spend <= $120k (target for customer approval)

Assumptions (explicit)\- Model family: open-weights 70B baseline (float16 runtime), fallback: 33B quantized int8 (latency/cost profile known)\- Typical prompt length: 800 tokens; average generated tokens: 120\- Traffic mix: 80% short chat (<= 128 tokens), 20% long-form generation\- Peak daily window: 11:00-14:00 local (35% of daily volume arrives here)\- Desired SLO at p95 for tail latency = 450ms; p99 target 1200ms\- Network egress negligible for cost model (prototype)

Workload profile (rough measured inputs)\- Baseline concurrency target: 180 concurrent inference sessions (steady)\- Short bursts modeled as Poisson arrivals with lambda adjusted to create 400 QPS for up to 30s\- Memory working set per session (KV cache + activation) ~ 26GB for 70B float16 with sequence length headroom\- 33B quantized working set (int8 variant) ~ 10GB

Sizing methodology (quick-run steps we used)
1) Determine per-GPU effective concurrent capacity: run microbenchmarks (local) to measure tokens/sec and maximum concurrent KV contexts while keeping generator latency < target. For this POC we used A100-80GB and H100-80GB profiles.
2) Choose a conservative packing factor: we assume 60% packing efficiency under mixed batch sizes (real-world jitter).
3) Convert concurrency target -> required number of replicas per model variant, include margin buffer for autoscale (headroom).
4) Design prewarm and burst pool: small hot pool of 10% of steady capacity reserved for ultra-low-latency; add a shared burst pool (on-demand) sized to absorb 200 QPS bursts.

Bench numbers (summarized testing)
- A100-80GB (70B float16): stable 15 concurrent sessions with p95=380ms at 50 tokens; tokens/sec ~ 1200 per GPU under continuous load\- H100-80GB (70B float16, kernel-optimized): stable 22 concurrent sessions p95=320ms; tokens/sec ~ 1750 per GPU\- A100-80GB (33B int8): stable 40 concurrent sessions p95=260ms; tokens/sec ~ 2600
Notes: these are lab profiles using continuous batching; real traffic suffers from fragmentation (hence packing factor).

Initial sizing (Minimum Viable Dedicated – Phase 1)\- Steady demand: 180 concurrent sessions mapped to 70B model: (using H100 effective concurrency 22 -> 180/22 = 8.2 -> round up 9 replicas)\- Packing factor 60% -> require 9 / 0.6 = 15 H100 GPUs for primary 70B pool (provides steady plus small buffer)\- Prewarm hot pool (low-latency): 10% of steady => 2 H100s (hot instances with warmed KV cache)\- Burst / overflow pool: allow fallback to 33B int8 on A100s (cheaper) sized to absorb additional 200 QPS bursts: observed concurrency for equivalent throughput -> 200 QPS at short tokens ~= 6 A100s (33B)
Total Phase 1 Fleet: 17 H100s + 6 A100s (33B fallback)

Autoscale and fallback policy (proposed)
- Primary autoscale (H100 70B): scale up by 1 replica when 10-min average CPU/GPU utilization > 68% or queue depth > 40 requests for > 45s. Scale-down after 20 min at utilization < 40%. Cooldown 8 minutes for small oscillations.
- Prewarm policy: keep hot pool warm during predictable window (09:30–16:00) and reduce to 1 hot node off-peak. Warm-up trigger: if projected short-term traffic (10-min EWMA) > 75% of hot pool capacity, spin hot nodes up from cold pool 90s before predicted spike.
- Burst routing: if request queue length crosses 120 requests and primary pool scaling exhausted (budget or max replicas), route new requests to 33B int8 replicas with an annotation marking lower-fidelity. Implement gradual traffic shaping with token budget to reduce user-visible quality drop.
- Canary fallback: for <=10% of routed fallback traffic, run shadow calls on both models and log divergence metrics for quality regressions.

Costing (prototype monthly estimate) - quick model
Assumptions:
- H100 instance effective hourly price (committed blend): $9.50/hr (reserved), A100 effective hourly: $4.00/hr (on burst pool cheaper reserved rate)\- Full-month hours: 730
Scenario A (conservative reserved commit matching Phase 1):
- 17 H100s reserved -> 17 * $9.50 * 730 = $118,235
- 6 A100s burst reserved -> 6 * $4.00 * 730 = $17,520
- Total infra reserved cost ~ $135,755/mo
Notes: this exceeds customer target of $120k by ~13%. Options to reduce below target listed in sensitivity below.

Sensitivity scenarios (quick knobs)
1) Commit fewer H100s + rely more on autoscale to on-demand H100s during rare peaks: keep 12 H100 reserved, autoscale add-on of up to 5 on-demand H100 at $16/hr. Cost estimate: 12*$9.5*730 + expected on-demand hours (peaks ~ 60hrs total across month * 5 * $16) + 6*$4*730 = 12*6935 + 4800 + 17520 = 83,220 + 4,800 + 17,520 = $105,540 -> comfortably under target but has risk of capacity throttling during sustained higher-than-modeled peaks.
2) Hybrid quantization path: push more traffic to 33B int8 by pre-qualifying requests (heuristic-based routing): require 35% of steady traffic to fall back to 33B. This reduces needed H100s to 11 and increases A100s to 12. Cost: 11*$9.5*730 + 12*$4*730 = 11*6935 + 12*2920 = 76,285 + 35,040 = $111,325.
3) Model-engine optimizations (kernel improvements): if H100 tokens/sec improves by 20% then effective concurrency jumps -> reduce H100 count from 17 to 13, cost -> 13*6935 + 6*2920 = 90,155 + 17,520 = $107,675.

Trade-offs and risks
- Overcommitting H100s drives cost above customer target but provides strong tail-latency guarantees.
- Relying on on-demand H100 for peaks is cost-efficient but risks elevated p95/p99 during capacity acquisition windows.
- Routing significant traffic to quantized 33B reduces cost but risks quality regressions; must back with shadowing and evals before enabling broadly.
- Cold start for large models (KV cache) can add 600–1500ms depending on sequence length; prewarm and hot pool mitigate this.

Operational playbook notes (short)
- Day 0: run 3 synthetic load profiles mirroring customer traffic, validate p95 and p99 with smoke tests; capture artifacts and perf traces to the console dashboards route: /projects/meridian/poc-logs.
- Day 1–7: observe real traffic, keep conservative reserved commit, adjust autoscale policy parameters (queue thresholds, EWMA windows).
- Metric dashboards to watch: per-replica tokens/sec, average KV hit-rate, new cold-start count, fallback ratio, latency-percentiles, and error/retry rate.

Quality & evals
- Create a small eval suite of 500 prompts sampled from customer's dataset; run daily shadow diffs comparing 70B -> 33B outputs and compute semantic similarity and accept/reject thresholds. If the rejection rate for 33B > 6% then reduce fallback routing by 50%.

Open questions / TODOs
- Get customer's true long-tail usage (per-customer/feature) to refine packing factor and prewarm sizing (action: ask CS for last 30 days logs)\- Confirm allowed fidelity loss for fallback; create a short rubric of routes safe to route to 33B (action: product + CS)\- Confirm committed pricing assumptions (finance) and whether market H100 reserved pricing can be negotiated for POC

Deliverables for the next meeting
- Slide: Executive 1-pager with options A/B/C and recommended path (decision trees and cost deltas)\- Small lab runbook with exact commands to spin the Phase 1 fleet and autoscale rules (repo PR: dedicated-config/pull/142)\- Sensitivity spreadsheet (sheet id placeholder linked_artifacts) with delta scenarios and break-even points

Notes to self (informal)
- If customer insists on p99 < 800ms, recommend 20% more hot pool and higher reserved commit.
- Watch out for multi-tenant admission if we want to consolidate cheaper GPU pools later; fragmentation kills packing.

References and links
- Linear ticket: RED-321 (linked above)\- Bench scripts: github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/meridian-poc

End of worksheet
